items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: We know definitely that King Oliver influenced Louis.

ctx.x: We know definitely that King Oliver influenced Louis. And others before King Oliver influenced him. It went on down the line, you see. But who did influence Bix with that sound?

Well, I guess a lot of musicians who have played with Hardy, I guess Ray Burt was one that played with him early. But I forgot what interview it was. They were talking about his sound being the pure New Orleans sound, but with a sweet tone that was not characteristic of New Orleans sound. But they say that Buddy Molden, too. But also that Emmett had played in Davenport for a while, and Bix had heard him there. And that he...

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: Maybe at some times, Emmett may have sounded like Bix, and then again, maybe at some times he may have played in the vein of King Oliver or Louis or something.

ctx.x: I want to get back to Dixon in the mist. How did he play on the piano? Did he play more or less legitimately or did he have unusual things?

Well you know, Dixon's piano playing was really amazing because in listening to Dixon's Bix playing piano, I can never really tie in his trumpet with the piano. I don't know if it ever struck you that way, Dick, but listening to his trumpet, it sounds like it's an entirely different phase than his piano playing. His piano sounds so different that it was rhythmical with really sort of modern chords and yet there was the old time flavor along with it. It's just a hard thing to explain, his piano playing. You know,…
Did you ever hear Brownlee's band? Norman Brownlee?
